prerequisites: Knowledge concerning: resolution of systems of linear algebraic equations and first-order linear differential equations, properties of trigonometric functions and operations on complex numbers.
Knowledge of the fundamentals of electromagnetism.

learning_outcomes.text: The student knows: methods for analyzing linear circuits, in steady-state, single-phase and three-phase sinusoidal regimes. Analysis of simple first and second order linear circuits in transient phase. Principle of operation and linear model of the transformer. Principle of operation and mechanical and electro-mechanical characteristics of induction and DC motors.

At the end of the course, the student is able to: analyze a linear circuit, in steady-state, single-phase and three-phase sinusoidal regimes, including an ideal transformer, simple first and second order transient circuits, and examine the mechanical and electromechanical characteristics of asynchronous and direct current motors.
To be able to identify the most appropriate method for analyzing a linear circuit and interpret the main electrical nameplate data of a motor.
To be able to describe, in written form, the procedure for analyzing a linear circuit. To be able to orally present a course topic.
To be able to apply the acquired knowledge to contexts different from those presented during the course, and to deepen the topics covered using materials different from those proposed.

syllabus_topics: BIPOLAR DEVICES. ENERGY AND PASSIVITY. KIRCHHOFF'S LAWS.
METHODS FOR SOLVING LINEAR NETWORKS. APPLICATION OF THEOREMS OF TELLEGEN, THÉVÉNIN, NORTON.
PHASORS. SYMBOLIC METHOD. IMPEDANCE. INSTANTANEOUS, ACTIVE AND REACTIVE POWER.
POWER CONSERVATION. POWER FACTOR CORRECTION. RESONANCE.
SYMMETRICAL THREE-PHASE SYSTEMS, BOTH BALANCED AND UNBALANCED. MEASUREMENT OF ACTIVE AND REACTIVE POWER IN THREE-PHASE SYSTEMS.
FIRST AND SECOND ORDER LINEAR CIRCUITS IN TRANSIENT PHASE. FREE EVOLUTION AND FORCED EVOLUTION. ZERO-STATE AND ZERO-INPUT SOLUTION.
SOFT AND HARD FERROMAGNETIC MATERIALS. PERMANENT MAGNETS. HYSTERESIS. EDDY CURRENTS. LOSSES. MAGNETIC CIRCUITS. RELUCTANCE. ELECTROMAGNETS. PRINCIPLES OF ELECTROMECHANICAL ENERGY CONVERSION.
CONCEPT OF TRANSFORMER. IDEAL TRANSFORMER. DC TRANSFORMER: DC/DC CONVERSION. AC TRANSFORMER. MUTUALLY COUPLED CIRCUITS. OPERATING PRINCIPLE. NO-LOAD, ON-LOAD AND SHORT-CIRCUIT OPERATION.
OPERATING PRINCIPLE OF ASYNCHRONOUS MOTOR AND DC MOTOR, MECHANICAL AND ELECTRO-MECHANICAL CHARACTERISTICS. COUPLING WITH A MECHANICAL LOAD.
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written test and an optional oral test. The written test lasts at least two hours and thirty minutes and consists of three exercises; the student must correctly answer at least the first question of each exercise. The exam is passed if the grade obtained in the written test is at least 18/30. Access to the oral test is conditional on passing the written test with a grade of at least 26/30. The minimum grade (18) is achieved by correctly answering the first question of each of the three exercises, taking into account the completeness and clarity of the solution. The maximum grade (30) is awarded to the student who demonstrates, through the written test alone or through integration with an oral test, the ability to apply the studied methods in different contexts. A distinction (Lode) is awarded to the candidate who also took the oral test, demonstrating significant mastery of theoretical and operational content, presenting arguments with notable linguistic proficiency and capacity for independent elaboration even in contexts different from those proposed by the lecturer.
